knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Elimination takes away what creates the danger and ranks first. The other options are lower on the hierarchy.
Protective equipment is at the bottom of the hierarchy. Isolation, substitution and engineering controls are higher.
A likely and severe risk needs escalation and controls under the organisation procedure. The other options avoid the assessment or misrate the risk.

practicalCriteria: Given a sample risk, the learner selects the likelihood and consequence categories and reads the rating from the organisation matrix.
Given three control options, the learner ranks them on the hierarchy and selects the highest control that suits the hazard.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed risk rating record for a simulated risk
Assessor record of the control ranking
stopWorkCriteria: A risk is rated high or extreme under the organisation matrix: stop, escalate to the supervisor, and do not continue until the procedure is followed.
The only control available is protective equipment for a hazard that a higher control could remove: stop and refer for a higher control.
